successors.text: the Philippine archipelago, as ceded by the Treaty of Paris

ledger.x: 11 April 1899: the Insular Government is established.
April 1899: the American claim is contested by the First Philippine Republic.
19 April 1901: the republic is dissolved de jure.
15 November 1935: the Commonwealth replaces the Insular Government.
May 1942: the rest of the archipelago is Japanese-held.
27 February 1945: Manila is back under the Commonwealth.
27 February 1945: the Commonwealth is restored at Manila.
2 September 1945: Japan's surrender ends the occupation.
4 July 1946: the Commonwealth, the last form of the American colonial government, ends with independence.

wars.name: Philippine-American War
wars.outcome: American victory: Malolos captured on 31 March 1899, Aguinaldo captured on 23 March 1901 and the republic dissolved de jure on 19 April 1901 (de facto 16 April 1902).

wars.name: Japanese invasion and occupation of the Philippines
wars.outcome: Japanese victory in May 1942 (final surrender of joint US-Philippine forces), then Allied reconquest: landing on Leyte on 20 October 1944, Manila retaken by 27 February 1945, surrender signed 2 September 1945.

certainty.note: The Americans held only part of the archipelago while the First Philippine Republic held most of it; the American claim covers the whole.
An archipelago ceded by treaty: its limits are the coasts; the Moro Province (Mindanao and Sulu) was governed within it.
A government in exile (from 12 March 1942) with the islands under Japanese occupation; the occupation events carry the land.
The coasts of the archipelago until independence on 4 July 1946.
